newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn stressed, soybeans unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn stressed, soybeans unchanged.

text.p: The condition of Indiana's corn declined slightly during the week ended Sunday because of hot, dry weather in many parts of the state, while soybeans were unchanged, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service weekly crop report.

Corn was rated 42 percent good to excellent versus 45 a week ago and 41 a year ago. Five percent of the corn was mature versus six a year ago and the 10 percent average. Eighty-two percent of the corn acreage reached the dough stage versus 93 a year ago and the 95 average.

Soybeans were rated 36 percent good to excellent, unchanged from a week ago but down from 46 percent a year ago. Three percent of the crop was shedding leaves versus seven a year ago and eight on average. Ninety-two percent were setting pods versus 98 a year ago and the 99 average.
Pastures were rated one percent excellent, 21 good, 41 fair, 22 poor and 15 very poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 34 adequate, 44 short, and 21 very short. Subsoil moisture was rated two percent surplus, 44 adequate, 43 short and 11 very short.
